_study: qal/strip -- static-CMOS stripping: nMOS tree + cross-coupled pMOS
_pre_registration: PRE_REGISTERED.json (sha256 in MTIMES.txt), the only file in this directory when it was written

LEAKAGE_dc._method: constant-bias transient read at a true steady state; .DC did not return under PyMS-compiled PSP103 and a ramp would inject ~40 nA of displacement current

LEAKAGE_hold._declared_bias: sg13lv_compat.sp zeroes ad/as/pd/ps: drain/source JUNCTION leakage is ABSENT, so every current here is a LOWER BOUND and the budget is OPTIMISTIC on leakage. The same omission removes drain junction CAPACITANCE, which makes the node LIGHTER than reality and therefore OVERSTATES the lost FRACTION -- that bias cuts the other way.

LEAKAGE_null_control._why: L3's 2 ns droop (575 nV) sits at the solver's own RELTOL voltage resolution (~557 nV on this rail), so a NULL control -- a 2 fF cap with nothing attached -- and a 100 ns hold are needed before any leakage number is quoted.
LEAKAGE_null_control._declared_bias: sg13lv_compat.sp zeroes ad/as/pd/ps: junction leakage is ABSENT, so all of this is a LOWER BOUND on real leakage.

LEAKAGE_gmin_floor._why: LEAK_DC's gate reading was exactly rail*1e-12 A, the signature of a 1e-12 S conductance. This deck measures what a known 1e12 ohm path looks like here (qref) and what a hard-off device (Vgs = -0.3 V) still shows (qhard), so the GMIN floor is bounded by measurement.
LEAKAGE_gmin_floor._direction_of_bias: any GMIN component INFLATES the measured leakage, so the leakage budget is an UPPER BOUND regardless of how the split lands.

RECEIVER._method: N independent receiver copies at constant input in one deck, read at a steady state; .DC does not return under PyMS-compiled PSP103 in this environment
RECEIVER._note: the stripped receiver is measured with BOTH output nodes initialised to 0 -- the real QAL condition, where the ramping rail precharges from zero -- so the number is the REGENERATIVE decision boundary of the cross-coupled pair, not a static inverter trip point

CROSSOVER._method:
(d, part 2) THE DEVICE-COUNT CROSSOVER, as a library rule rather than six
anecdotes.

For every family of the committed qal/sha256 mapped-netlist census, the factored
series-parallel nMOS tree of f and of f-bar is written down, VERIFIED EXHAUSTIVELY
against that cell's own truth table from qal/sha256/cells/stack_depths.json, and
counted.  The static count is the PDK cell's own device count from
qal/sha256/cells/cell_widths.json.

  stripped = n(tree f) + n(tree f-bar) + 2
  static   = n_nmos + n_pmos                     (the PDK cell as shipped)

For a single-stage complementary CMOS gate realising a series-parallel function,
n_nmos = n_pmos = N and the two trees of the stripped form are duals of the same
size, so stripped - static = 2 - ovh where ovh is whatever the PDK cell spends
BEYOND one complementary pair -- an internal inverter, an output stage, an input
inverter.  The crossover is therefore at ovh = 2, and it is a statement about
INVERSION OVERHEAD, not about gate complexity.

RULE.arithmetic: stripped - static = 2 - ovh, ovh = static devices beyond one complementary pair of the factored tree

CELLFLOOR._method:
THE CELL FLOOR -- stripped vs static on an IDEAL STIFF RAIL.

Every row in st.py couples two things that must be separated before any verdict:

  (1) the CELL's own ability to settle at a given rail, and
  (2) what rail the bank actually gets, which depends on the bank's load against
      a source tank this study holds FIXED at the committed 35.979 fF.

A stripped bank has twice as many output nodes as a static one, so at a fixed
tank it is delivered a LOWER rail -- measured at 48-159 mV lower depending on
the family.  That depresses the pull-up's overdrive (rail - |Vtp|) and is a
property of the harness's fixed tank, not of the topology: a designer would
size the tank to the bank.

This deck removes (2) entirely.  The rail is an IDEAL voltage source stepped to
a chosen level and held there; there is no tank, no inductor, no transfer switch
and nothing to droop.  Inputs are RAIL-REFERENCED (vin = rail), the realistic
chain condition, not the committed 1.5 V drive.  What is left is (1) alone: at
this rail, does this cell settle, and how fast.

This is the same instrument qal/skip4's skeptic used to show that every beat
<= 160 ps was already impossible at a chain-delivered rail for reasons having
nothing to do with the power schedule.

P1_o21ai_equivalent_settles.verdict: CONFIRMED UNDER THE COMMITTED INPUT CONVENTION, REFUTED UNDER RAIL-REFERENCED INPUTS
P1_o21ai_equivalent_settles.detail: At the committed bank convention (inputs driven at dV = 1.5 V) and the cross-coupled pMOS at 1.12 um, the stripped o21ai-equivalent SETTLES: t_valid90 = 452.6 ps, all 16 checked nodes 94.26-101.50% of the instantaneous rail, where static sg13g2_o21ai_1 never reaches 90% (82.99% asymptote, t_valid80 = 515.1 ps). With inputs at the delivered rail (0.6077 V) instead, the same cell reaches only 51.33-66.81% and the static control reaches 99.14%. The pre-registered PRIMARY sizing (wxc = 0.56 um) FAILS (75.46%); the pre-registered CONTROL (1.12 um) is what passes.

P2_device_count_crossover.detail: stripped - static = 2 - ovh, verified for all 13 census families with every series-parallel tree checked exhaustively against that cell's own PDK truth table (0 mismatches). Loses by 2: inv, nand2, nor2, o21ai, a21oi. Ties: buf, and2, or2, nor2b, xnor2, xor2, a21o. Wins by 2: mux2 only. The crossover is INVERSION OVERHEAD, not gate complexity.

P3_pullup_Vgs.verdict: CONFIRMED WHEN THE PAIR RESOLVES; DEGRADES WHEN IT DOES NOT
P3_pullup_Vgs.detail: Stripped pull-up: Vgs = -1.0001 to -1.0011 x rail at the end, -0.9409 x rail at the conduction instant, Vbs = 0.0000 V exactly at every instant (source and bulk are the same node by construction). Pre-registered claim was >= 0.95 x rail at conduction: measured 0.941, marginally short, >= 0.96 at every later instant. Static o21ai binding series pMOS: -0.8516 x rail at conduction with +0.1183 V reverse body bias. BUT in the rows where the cross-coupled pair fails to resolve (rail-referenced inputs) the stripped pull-up's Vgs falls to -0.69 to -0.76 x rail, i.e. no better than the static series device.

P4_droop.detail: Worst per-node droop over a 200 ps beat anywhere in 22 rows is 18.386 mV (the settling stripped o21ai, nodes with a 309.9 ps hold window); most nodes 0-5.4 mV. Pre-registered < 5 mV was right for the typical node and optimistic by ~3.7x for the worst. A5 PASSES on every node of every row against this study's own measured 75.33 mV receiver window. NOTE the RAIL droops 35-218 mV over the same beat -- up to 11.9x the worst node -- and no output keeper can fix that, because a keeper is referenced to the same drooping rail.

P5_leakage.detail: Measured total current off a real held stripped-cell node (OFF tree nMOS + OFF opposite cross-coupled pMOS, 2 fF at 0.6077 V) = 0.6226 pA, an UPPER BOUND: a known 1e12 ohm resistor reads 0.6077 pA in this harness and a hard-off device (Vgs = -0.3 V) reads 0.3062 pA, so at least half is the simulator's conductance floor. Pre-registered guess was 0.1-10 nA; measured is 1606x below the brief's assumed 1 nA.

P6_chain.detail: The stripped chain holds per-gate values only at depth 1 (7/8 correct, separation 305.9 mV = 47.5x the 6.44 mV floor, driven by ideal head sources). From depth 2 onward separation is NEGATIVE (-28.6, -5.9, -3.5, -3.3, -0.9 mV) and only 4/8 nodes are on the correct side, which is what an unresolved dual-rail pair gives by construction. The STATIC control chain keeps separation POSITIVE at every depth (269.8 -> 294.9 -> 113.5 -> 88.0 -> 34.7 -> 51.4 mV, 5.4-45.8x floor) but its per-gate values are wrong at 5 of 6 depths -- ordering survives, levels do not. So on the chain the stripped form is WORSE than the static control it was meant to replace.

PREREGISTERED_RISK_OUTCOMES.R1_contention: NOT the failure mode. Every pull-DOWN node settles to 100.01-100.12% -- the trees win the contention easily. The pair does not sit metastable at mid-rail in the single-hop rows.
PREREGISTERED_RISK_OUTCOMES.R2_crowbar: NOT dominant. The stripped cell's total metered energy per operation is 4.122 fJ vs 6.071 fJ for the static o21ai under the committed convention, and 3.146 vs 2.554 fJ under rail-referenced inputs -- so it is cheaper under one convention and 23% dearer under the other, not catastrophically crowbarred.
PREREGISTERED_RISK_OUTCOMES.R3_nMOS_is_the_new_wall: REALISED, AND IT IS THE HEADLINE. Vtn = 0.5239460 V is 83.7 mV HIGHER than |Vtp| = 0.4402734 V (both MEASURED). Putting the whole logic function into nMOS trees moves the burden onto the device with 83.7 mV LESS headroom. At the stripped bank's own delivered rail of 0.5240 V the tree nMOS overdrive is +0.1 mV -- exactly at threshold. This, not contention and not crowbar, is why rail-referenced inputs and the chain fail.
PREREGISTERED_RISK_OUTCOMES.R4_latch_is_a_holding_path: STANDS AS STATED. The cross-coupled pair is a latch. What the run shows removable is the KEEPER (measured: 62.5 nV of droop over a beat on a bare node, keeper benefit below the measurement floor) and the PRECHARGE device (the ramping rail precharges both nodes from 0 -- no precharge device appears in any deck). The holding function is moved into 2 devices, not eliminated.
PREREGISTERED_RISK_OUTCOMES.R5_dual_rail_wiring: UNMEASURED as declared. Device count does not capture that every net becomes two wires. What IS measured is the electrical half of that cost: the stripped bank puts twice as many output nodes on one tank and is delivered a rail 48-159 mV lower at a FIXED 35.979 fF tank.

_limitations: Only the o21ai family was measured at the corrected cross-coupled pMOS width (1.12 um). inv, nand2, nor2, xnor2 and mux2 were measured only at the pre-registered 0.56 um, which the o21ai sweep shows is under-sized; those five stripped rows therefore UNDERSTATE the topology and must not be read as its ceiling.

The single-hop harness gives a 500 ps settling tail. The cell-floor deck (ideal rail, 3 ns window) shows the stripped cell needs 1.2-2.7 ns at rail-referenced input levels, so a 'NEVER' in the single-hop table and a finite number in the cell-floor table are the same fact seen through different windows.
Four of eight expected-HIGH nodes in the settling stripped row were still rising at the end of the tail, so they have no measurable hold window and contribute no droop number.

The receiver trip measured here (0.4932 x rail at 0.6077 V, 0.5467 x rail at 1.0 V) does not reproduce the campaign's quoted ~0.59 x rail at the QAL rail, though it is close at 1.0 V. At rails <= 0.56 V the static inverter receiver's own pull-up sits at or below |Vtp| so its DC curve never traverses the rail and a trip point is not well-defined. Both numbers are reported; the disagreement is not resolved.

The chain was run at ONE operating point (the committed banktank headline m=10/T=200/H=4/dv=1.2) and at one stripped sizing. No chain was run at the under-sized 0.56 um (started, then abandoned and restarted at 1.12 um; ~2 probes of work discarded).

Junction leakage is absent (shim zeroes ad/as/pd/ps). Bounded from the model card at ~2.0e-20 A on ASSUMED diffusion geometry, ~7 orders below the measured subthreshold path -- DERIVED from ASSUMED, not measured.
CELLFLOOR.json contains one duplicated static row at rail 0.5217 V, left by the first (crashed) invocation before the device-count fix; it is the same measurement, not an independent one.
